'''''Eucomis autumnalis''''', the '''autumn pineapple flower''', or '''autumn pineapple lily''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asparagaceae]], subfamily [[Scilloideae]], [[native plant|native]] to Malawi, Zimbabwe and southern Africa. It is a mid to late summer flowering [[deciduous]] [[bulbous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]]. The flower stem reaches about {{convert|40|cm|0|abbr=on}}, rising from a basal [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]] of wavy-edged leaves. The green, yellow or white flowers are arranged in a spike ([[raceme]]), topped by a "head" of green leaflike bracts. It is grown as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental garden plant]] and can also be used as a [[cut flower]].

==Description==
''Eucomis autumnalis'' is a [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing from a large [[bulb]] with a diameter of up to {{cvt|8|–|10|cm|in|frac=4}}. Like other ''Eucomis'' species, it has a basal rosette of strap-shaped leaves. These are up to {{cvt|55|cm|in|0}} long and {{cvt|6|–|13|cm|in|frac=2}} wide, with a wavy margin. The sweetly scented [[inflorescence]], produced in late summer, is a dense [[raceme]], reaching an overall height of {{cvt|30|-|45|cm|ftin|0}}. The individual flowers have green, yellow-green or white [[tepal]]s and are borne on short stalks ([[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]]) {{cvt|2|–|10|mm|in|frac=8}} long. The filaments of the [[stamen]]s are joined at the base to form a slightly cup-shaped structure. The inflorescence is topped by a head (coma) of green bracts, up to {{cvt|65|mm|in|frac=2}} long. The plant has no purple coloration.<ref name=Comp90/><ref name=APD_176472/> The structure of the seed capsule distinguishes the two subspecies: ''E. autumnalis'' subsp. ''autumnalis'' has a thin-walled and often somewhat inflated capsule; ''E. autumnalis'' subsp. ''clavata'' has a capsule with a hard double-layered wall ([[Fruit anatomy#Pericarp layers|pericarp]]).<ref name=Comp90/> It also has a somewhat club-shaped (clavate) [[Scape (botany)|scape]],<ref name=APD_14630/> narrowing towards the base.<ref name=Crou10/>

==Taxonomy==
''Eucomis autumnalis'' was first described by [[Philip Miller]] in 1768, as ''Fritillaria autumnalis''. It was formally transferred to ''Eucomis'' by [[Frederick James Chittenden]] in 1951.<ref name=POWO/> The specific epithet ''autumnalis'' refers to its flowering and fruiting time, and distinguishes it from ''[[Eucomis regia]]'' which flowers in early spring.<ref name=Comp90/> It is one of a group of larger [[tetraploid]] species of ''[[Eucomis]]'', with 2''n'' = 4''x'' = 60.<ref name=ZonnDunc10/>

===Subspecies===
The species includes two subspecies:<ref name=POWO/>
* ''Eucomis autumnalis'' subsp. ''autumnalis''
* ''Eucomis autumnalis'' subsp. ''clavata'' {{small|(Baker) Reyneke}}
''E. undulata'' (the specific epithet referring to the wavy-edged leaves) is a name sometimes used,<ref name=Comp90/> but is now regarded as a synonym of ''E. autumnalis'' subsp. ''autumnalis''.<ref name="POWO subsp.autumnalis"/>
An earlier recognized subspecies, ''E. autumnalis'' subsp. ''amaryllidifolia'',<ref name=plantzafrica/> is now accepted as a separate species, ''[[Eucomis amaryllidifolia]]''.

==Distribution and habitat==
''Eucomis autumnalis'' is found from [[Malawi]] to the [[Cape Provinces]] of South Africa.<ref name=POWO/> ''E. autumnalis'' subsp. ''autumnalis'' has been recorded from Malawi, [[Zimbabwe]], and, in South Africa, from the [[Northern Provinces]], the [[Free State (province)|Free State]] and the [[Cape Provinces]].<ref name="POWO subsp.autumnalis"/> ''E. autumnalis'' subsp. ''clavata'' has a more central distribution, being found in [[Botswana]], [[Eswatini]], [[Lesotho]], [[KwaZulu-Natal]], the Free State and the Northern Provinces.<ref name="POWO subsp.clavata"/>

''E. autumnalis'' subsp. ''clavata'' tends to be found at high altitudes.<ref name=APD_14630/> On the [[Drakensberg|Drakensberg escarpment]], it grows in grassland at {{cvt|3000|m|ft|-2}} where it is subject to cold winters and exposure.<ref name=Comp90/>

==Cultivation==
''Eucomis autumnalis'' is grown as an [[ornamental plant]]. The flowers and later the fruiting stems remain decorative for many weeks, and can be used as [[cut flowers]]. ''E. autumnalis'' survives frosts down to about {{cvt|-7|C|F|0}}, particularly if planted in a sheltered position in well-drained soil, kept as dry as possible during the winter dormancy. It grows and flowers best planted in full sun or partial shade in a fertile soil, and kept well watered during the summer period of growth and flowering.<ref name=plantzafrica/>

A [[cultivar]] is available under the name "''E. autumnalis'' 'White Dwarf'".<ref name=Crowders/> However, {{as of|2018|lc=yes}}, the ''RHS Plant Finder'' regards this as a cultivar of ''[[Eucomis zambesiaca|E. zambesiaca]]'' rather than ''E. autumnalis''.<ref name=RHSPF/>

===Propagation===
''Eucomis autumnalis'' can be propagated from seed sown in spring, but may take up to five seasons to flower. The bulb may produce [[offset (botany)|offset]]s, which can be removed while the plant is dormant. The bulblets can then be planted the following spring. [[Cutting (plant)|Leaf cuttings]] can be taken while the plant is in active growth. If sections of {{cvt|5|cm|in|0}} each are planted in sterilised and well-drained soil and kept in a humid environment, tiny bulbs should form within a few months. Sterilised bulb scales, leaf bases or flower stalks can also be used in [[Plant tissue culture|tissue culture]].<ref name=plantzafrica/>

== Chemistry ==
Various [[homoisoflavonoid]]s have been isolated from this plant.<ref name=SidwTamm70/>
